facts.fact_text: According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), she had read on various online social networks that many people intended to stage solo demonstrations (одиночные пикеты) on 19 December 2012 in front of the State Duma.

According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), the intended solo demonstrations on 19 December 2012 were to express opposition to the draft law prohibiting adoption of Russian children by United States citizens.
All three applicants decided to hold solo demonstrations on 19 December 2012.
According to the applicants, at around 9 a.m. on 19 December 2012 they positioned themselves, holding banners, in the vicinity of the State Duma.
According to the applicants, at around 9 a.m. on 19 December 2012 they were positioned at some distance from other protesters in the vicinity of the State Duma.
According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), she was arrested by the police several minutes after positioning herself near the State Duma on 19 December 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), after her arrest she was taken to a police van.
According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), there were no orders from police officers to stop the demonstration and leave the area before her arrest.

According to the second applicant (Ms Astakhova) and the third applicant (Ms Fokht-Babushkina), after their solo demonstrations they left the area, showing their posters to journalists at the journalists' request.
According to the second applicant (Ms Astakhova) and the third applicant (Ms Fokht-Babushkina), at the point when they were showing their posters to journalists, they were arrested by the police.
According to the second applicant (Ms Astakhova) and the third applicant (Ms Fokht-Babushkina), after their arrest they were taken to the Tverskoy district police station.

According to the Government, at 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the applicants were arrested and taken to the Tverskoy district police station for the purpose of compiling an administrative-offence record.
According to the Government, at 1.20 p.m. on 19 December 2012 the applicants were released from the Tverskoy district police station.
The format of solo demonstrations was chosen because there was no longer time to observe the minimum statutory three-day notification period required for other types of group public events.

Since 6 January 2013, Moscow City Law no. 10 of 4 April 2007 provides that the distance between solo demonstrations should be no less than fifty metres.

Moscow City Law no. 10 of 4 April 2007 specifies, in section 2.3, that simultaneous demonstrations should be treated as solo demonstrations, provided that they do not have a common goal and organisation.

According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), there were no orders from police officers to stop the demonstration and leave the area before her arrest.
According to the Government, at 10 a.m. on 19 December 2012 all three applicants took part in a group picket (пикет) held without prior notification of the authorities.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Ms Makarova) held a poster reading 'I am looking for an American who will adopt me' during the group picket on 19 December 2012.

According to the Government, the second applicant (Ms Astakhova) held a poster reading 'Orphans are guilty for the death of Mr Magnitskiy? Do not disgrace yourself' during the group picket on 19 December 2012.

According to the Government, the third applicant (Ms Fokht-Babushkina) held a poster reading 'Orphans are guilty for the death of Mr Magnitskiy? Do not disgrace yourself' during the group picket on 19 December 2012.
According to the Government, the applicants did not react to the lawful demands of the police to stop participating in the group picket on 19 December 2012.
According to the Government, the applicants continued picketing and attracted the attention of passers-by on 19 December 2012.

According to the Government, at 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the applicants were arrested and taken to the Tverskoy district police station for the purpose of compiling an administrative-offence record.

In the third applicant's (Ms Fokht-Babushkina's) appeal case, the appellate court examined some documents and interviewed a police officer in a detailed manner before affording the defence counsel an opportunity to cross-examine him.
In the third applicant's (Ms Fokht-Babushkina's) appeal case, the appeal judge asked a number of follow-up questions after the defence counsel cross-examined the police officer.

In its appeal decision in the third applicant's (Ms Fokht-Babushkina's) case, the Tverskoy District Court of Moscow considered that the third applicant's guilt had been proved by adverse evidence, including the administrative-offence record, the escort procedure record, and testimonies.
